entries: Starting at 5th level, when you use Spell Channeling, you can make two melee weapon attacks, instead of one. The second attack must target a different creature than the first. The effects of the spell are only triggered on the first hit.
At 11th level, both melee weapon attacks can target the same creature.

classFeaturesFull.name: Null Arcane
entries: At 6th level, you have learned to tap into the Void between planes. When you see a creature within 60 feet of you casting a spell of 5th level or lower, you can use your reaction to produce a field of opposing magic, nullifying the effect. You expend a number of arcana points equal to the spell's point cost, as shown in the Arcana Point Cost table (or 1 point for a cantrip) and make an Intelligence check. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a success, the creature's spell fails and has no effect.

classFeaturesFull.name: Planar Order Feature
entries: At 7th level, you gain a feature granted by your Planar Order.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeaturesFull.name: Planar Order Feature
entries: At 10th level, you gain a feature granted by your Planar Order.

classFeaturesFull.name: Combat Channeling Improvement
entries: At 11th level, both melee weapon attacks can target the same creature.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeaturesFull.name: Greater Focus
entries: Starting at 14th level, you gain the following Planar Focus options:

entries.name: Limbo
entries: Once per turn when you deal damage to a hostile creature with a melee weapon attack, you can use your bonus action to sap some arcane energy from the strike. On a hit, you regain 1 arcana point, up to your arcana point maximum.

entries.name: Paradise
entries: You have a flight speed equal to your movement speed. When you begin your turn in the air, you can maintain this effect by spending an arcana point. Otherwise, you fall.

entries.name: Underworld
entries: You can cast the spell {@spell vampiric touch} without using arcana points. You maintain {@condition concentration} on this spell as long as you maintain this planar focus.

classFeaturesFull.name: Planar Order Feature
entries: At 15th level, you gain a feature granted by your Planar Order.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeaturesFull.name: Planeshifter
entries: Starting at 18th level, you can freely walk the planes. You can cast the {@spell plane shift} spell once, without using arcana points or spell components.
Once you use this ability, you must finish a long rest before using it again.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeaturesFull.name: Nexus Arcane
entries: At 20th level, you connect with the central nexus of all existence. When you roll initiative and have no arcana points remaining, you immediately regain 10 arcana points.

entries.name: Channeler
entries: Squalid masses crowd draw close around a young Working furtively with chalk, incense, and an immense tome of diagrams, a bespectacled gnome traces a circle of the floor. With a flick of his wrist, the tile floor vanishes, unveiling a field engulfed in flames and a metallic metallic city looming in the distance.

A figure clad in a hooded azure robe draws a {@item longsword|PHB}, hefts it high in one hand, and vanishes. Appearing across the room an instant later, she brings the blade crashing down on a dragon's head, releasing a hail of blood and sparks.

Skilled in sword and spell alike, channelers are dynamic and formidable mages who draw their power from the planes of the multiverse. This connection stems from a unique arcane focus, called a portal key, through which they can unlock the doors of the universe.

entries.name: Key Bound
entries: The multiverse is crisscrossed by portals, passageways between the planes known only to a select few. Most are completely innocuous—archways, standing stones, ladders, and crawl spaces—until united with a specific magic item, a portal key. At that moment, the portal animates in a dance of arcane energy and twisting spacetime, transporting anyone nearby across the multiverse. These portals and their associated keys are deeply magical, intertwined with the energies of the planes themselves.

Channelers use these very portal keys as the source of their arcane magic. With one in hand, a channeler can call upon the very tides of the multiverse to fuel their arcana; without one, they have no magic to call their own.

entries.name: Walking the Multiverse
entries: Orders of channelers are perhaps the only organizations to possess a comprehensive understanding of the multiverse, its structure, and the portals which weave throughout it. Even the most intrepid explorer will become hopelessly lost among the infinite planes without expert guidance leading them to the right portals. By contrast, a channeler can travel unhindered, using their bound portal key to access a slew of portals known only to them and their order. Most channelers even learn of a few backdoors and side streets between the planes of existence, which they keep secret, in case they ever need to (for example) slip incognito to or from the Elemental Plane of Fire.

entries.name: Swordmages
entries: Channelers blur the line between spellcaster and warrior, marrying arcane might with physical prowess. Because all channelers are bound to a portal key, they have the innate potential to focus their spellcasting potential though other objects, and many seek to master the delicate art of balancing a spell's fury on the edge of a blade. Consequently, their strikes bite not only with steel, but also with flame, lightning, and frost.

entries.name: Creating a Channeler
entries: As you build your channeler, consider what entangled your character with extraplanar powers in the first place. Were you drawn to the vast, unending reaches of the distant Elemental Planes, or were you initiated into an order of channelers, before you truly understood their reach? Perhaps you accidentally became stranded in a city positioned between the planes, or in the shallowest layer of the Hells, before learning to walk the multiverse.

Also consider what type of portal key you bonded to, and what it says about your character. How did you acquire your key, and to which portal was it originally bound? If your key is a weapon, is it a family heirloom, a trophy taken from victorious combat, or a rusted piece of junk? If your key is a tome, what kind of book is it, and what information, other than spells and arcane secrets, is held within its pages? Perhaps, your key isn't an item of substantial importance; that too, is an important character note.

entries.name: Quick Build
entries: When building a channeler, you need to balance your physical and mental ability scores to maximize your character's potential. Your highest ability score should be Strength or Dexterity, followed by Intelligence. Your next highest ability score should be Constitution. Then, choose the Order of Blinknights and select the cantrips minor illusion and shocking grasp. Finally, choose any background and a versatile martial weapon as part of your equipment.

{@i Choose A or B} (A) 2 {@item Dagger|XPHB|Daggers}, {@item Leather Armor|XPHB}, {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}, {@item Alchemist's Fire|XPHB}, {@item Scholar's Pack|XPHB}, and 6 GP; or (B) 160 GP

classFeaturesFull.name: Bombs
entries: You can create volatile alchemical {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bombs} using the statistics shown in the Bomb sidebar.

entries.name: Bomb Mastery
entries: You have proficiency with {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bombs} and you can use the {@itemMastery Explode|ValdaGunslinger|Bomb's mastery property}.

entries.name: Intelligent Explosions
entries: When you use the {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bomb's} {@itemMastery Explode|ValdaGunslinger} property, you can gain a bonus to the damage roll equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

entries.name: Alchemist Save DC
entries: Some of your Alchemist features require your target to make a saving throw. The save DC equals 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You can use this save DC for your {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bombs} instead of the DC specified in the {@itemMastery Explode|ValdaGunslinger} property.

entries.name: How Many Bombs Do I Have?
entries: As an Alchemist, you can use {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} to effectively make as many {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bombs} as you need for the adventuring day at no cost. If you prefer to track your inventory of {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bombs} manually, you can create a number of {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bombs} equal to 10 + twice your Alchemist level when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. After 24 hours, an unused {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24} becomes inert.

classFeaturesFull.name: Reagents
entries: You have a collection of powerful reagents that you use to brew potions and fuel other Alchemist features. You have 2 Reagents. You regain one expended Reagent when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended Reagents when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You gain additional Reagents as you gain Alchemist levels, as shown in the Reagents column of the Alchemist Features table.

classFeaturesFull.name: Potion Brewing
entries: You can spend 10 minutes and expend any number of {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1} to brew potions, which can be done during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}. The number of {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1} and the Alchemist level required to brew a potion are given on the Potions table. You can have a total number of potions at one time up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). These potions retain potency until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, after which they become inert.

When you brew potions, you can also distill potions you have already brewed, destroying them and recovering the {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1} expended to brew them, up to a maximum of the number of {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1} listed on the Alchemist Features table. You can expend these {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1} immediately to brew new potions.
Your potions don't have unpredictable effects if a creature drinks one of your potions while still under the effects of another.

classFeaturesFull.name: Prime Bomb
entries: Once per turn when you hit with a {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24} or use the {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bomb's} {@itemMastery Explode|ValdaGunslinger} property, you can expend 1 {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1||Reagent} to add {@dice 1d10} to the {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bomb's} damage roll. When you reach certain Alchemist levels, you can expend more {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1}, up to the number shown in the Prime Bomb column of the Alchemist Features table, adding {@damage 1d10} damage for each {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1||Reagent} expended.

If you use the {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bomb's} {@itemMastery Explode|ValdaGunslinger} property, you can also increase the radius of the explosion up to 5 feet for each {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1||Reagent} expended in this way. For example, if you expend 2 {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1} at Alchemist level 5, the {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24} deals an extra {@damage 2d10} damage and you can choose for the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} to be a 5, 10 or 15-foot-radius.

classFeaturesFull.name: Bomb Formulas
entries: Your research has uncovered new formulations for your Bombs that you can apply just before throwing them. Choose three Bomb Formulas from the "{@filter Bomb Formula Options|optionalfeatures|feature type=bf}" section later in this class's description.

entries.name: Replacing and Gaining Formulas
entries: When you reach certain Alchemist levels, you learn additional formulas of your choice, as shown in the Formulas column of the Alchemist Features table. Additionally, whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace one of your Bomb Formulas with another formula of your choice. If another Alchemist feature gives you a Bomb Formula, it doesn't count against your number of formulas.

entries.name: Applying Bomb Formulas
entries: Once per turn when you attack with a {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24} or use the {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bomb's} {@itemMastery Explode|ValdaGunslinger} property, you can apply a Bomb Formula to it. Some Bomb Formulas change the Bomb's damage dice and damage type, including Improved Bombs damage starting at Alchemist level 5. Bomb Formulas don't change the size of the extra damage dice from {@classFeature Prime Bomb|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|2}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Reagent Synthesis
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can regain an additional number of expended {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1} up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Alchemist Subclass
entries: You gain an Alchemist subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Alchemist levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Alchemist level or lower.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Discovery
entries: In the course of your research, you have made a number of Discoveries regarding the nature of alchemy. You gain one Discovery of your choice from the "{@filter Discovery Options|optionalfeatures|source=|feature type=do}" section later in this class's description.

You gain another Discovery at Alchemist levels 9, 13, and 17. You can't pick the same Discovery more than once. Whenever you gain an Alchemist level, you can replace one of your Discoveries with another one for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Improved Bombs
entries: Once per turn when you deal damage with a {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24}, you can improve its damage dice to {@dice 2d10}. This damage further improves at certain Alchemist levels as shown in the Bomb Damage column of the Alchemist Features table.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Alchemist Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Evasion
entries: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail.
You don't benefit from this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Discovery
entries: You gain another {@classFeature Discovery|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|5}. You can't pick the same {@classFeature Discovery|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|5} more than once. Whenever you gain an Alchemist level, you can replace one of your {@classFeature Discovery|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|5||Discoveries} with another one for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Alchemist Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Blast Coating
entries: You automatically succeed on saving throws against your own {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bombs} and never take damage from them.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Discovery
entries: You gain another {@classFeature Discovery|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|5}. You can't pick the same {@classFeature Discovery|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|5} more than once. Whenever you gain an Alchemist level, you can replace one of your {@classFeature Discovery|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|5||Discoveries} with another one for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Alchemist Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Potion Mixologist
entries: You can mix two potions together and drink them as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, gaining the effects of both. You suffer no unexpected effects from mixing potions.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Discovery
entries: You gain another {@classFeature Discovery|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|5}. You can't pick the same {@classFeature Discovery|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|5} more than once. Whenever you gain an Alchemist level, you can replace one of your {@classFeature Discovery|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|5||Discoveries} with another one for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Experimentalist
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace any of your Bomb Formulas with other formulaa of your choice, and you can replace one of your discoveries with another one for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Philosopher's Stone
entries: You gain the crowning achievement of alchemy: a Philosopher's Stone, a dynamo of alchemical energy in a fist-sized, glowing jewel.

entries.name: Constructing a New Philosopher's Stone
entries: If your Philosopher's Stone is destroyed, you can construct a new one using {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}, materials worth 1,000+ GP, and 7 days of work. You can only have one Philosopher's Stone at a time.

entries.name: Philosopher's Stone Benefits
entries: As long as you possess the stone, you gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Regenerating Reagents
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you regain expended {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1} until you have 6 if you have 5 or fewer.

entries.name: Quick Brewing
entries: You can brew potions as a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, instead of over the course of 10 minutes.

entries.name: Longevity
entries: For every ten years that pass, your body ages only one year.

classFeaturesFull.name: Nuclear Bomb
entries: You can utilize the most devastating Bomb Formula imaginable. By replacing your {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bomb's} explosive contents with your Philosopher's Stone, you can change it into a Nuclear Bomb. You must use the {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bomb's} {@itemMastery Explode|ValdaGunslinger} property. This Bomb deals {@damage 10d10 + 100} Force damage instead of its normal Fire damage, and its explosion is a {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} with a radius of 1 mile.
This {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24} completely destroys your Philosopher's Stone.

entries.name: Alchemist
entries: Whether their methods are explosive, transformative, or restorative, Alchemists transmute the world around them to their liking.

entries.name: Explosive Reactions
entries: One of the first things an Alchemist learns is which chemicals react explosively with one other. Ostensibly, this is to prevent deadly accidents, but adventuring Alchemists regularly apply this knowledge to create {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bombs}.

An alchemical bomb is a one-pound, apple-sized, spherical glass or clay flask filled with a reactive chemical. A smaller vial of thin glass containing a reagent is suspended in the liquid, and the whole thing is sealed with a cork or wax seal. When the inner vial breaks, usually on impact, the chemicals react with a violent explosion. With experimentation, an Alchemist can even infuse these explosions with elemental fire, lightning, or frost.

entries.name: Serums and Tinctures
entries: Experienced Alchemists learn to brew potions, alchemical concoctions that replicate magical effects. These range from the medicinal, such as {@item Potions of Healing|XDMG}, to the transformative, such as {@item Potion of Gaseous Form|XDMG|Potions of Gaseous Form}. Undisputed masters of potion-brewing, an adventuring Alchemist should have a surplus of potions to distribute among their allies.

entries.name: Elemental Sciences
entries: The source of alchemy's power is the Elemental Planes. Therefore, it is no surprise that Alchemists strive to tap deeper into that power, researching and discovering new elemental compounds. The pinnacle of alchemy is the Philosopher's Stone, which is rumored to grant its bearer supreme command of the elements. Few Alchemists have succeeded in creating a Philosopher's Stone, and fewer still remain alive to divulge its secrets.

{@i Choose A, B, or C:} (A) {@item Chain Shirt|XPHB}, {@item Shield|XPHB}, {@item Longsword|XPHB}, 6 {@item Javelin|XPHB|Javelins}, {@item Explorer's Pack|XPHB}, and 54 GP; (B) {@item Studded Leather Armor|XPHB}, 2 {@item Shortsword|XPHB|Shortswords}, {@item Longbow|XPHB}, 20 {@item Arrow|XPHB|Arrows}, {@item Quiver|XPHB}, {@item Explorer's Pack|XPHB}, and 11 GP; or (C) 140 GP

classFeaturesFull.name: Battle Tactics
entries: You learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called Battle Dice.

entries.name: Battle Dice
entries: You have two Battle Dice, which are d6s. A Battle Die is expended when you use it. You regain all expended Battle Dice when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} or finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Your Battle Die changes and more Battle Dice become available as shown on the Battle Dice column of the Captain Features table.

entries.name: Maneuvers
entries: You can expend Battle Dice to perform maneuvers. Your maneuver options are detailed later in the class description.

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries: If a maneuver requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties} of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as {@item Lance|XPHB|Lances} and {@item Longsword|XPHB|Longswords}.
Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

classFeaturesFull.name: Cohort
entries: You gain a loyal Cohort who carries your banner and follows your lead.

entries.name: Initiating a Cohort
entries: Choose your {@filter Cohort's stat block|bestiary|tag=cohort} from those listed later in the class description. Following an 8-hour initiation period, which can be done during a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, that creature becomes your Cohort until you initiate a new Cohort to replace it. You can have only one Cohort at a time.

entries.name: Cohort in Combat
entries: Your Cohort is {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you and your allies and obeys your commands. In combat, your Cohort takes its turn immediately before or after your turn each round (your choice). Your Cohort uses your Charisma for its attack and damage rolls.

entries.name: Cohort Save DC
entries: If your Cohort forces a creature to make a saving throw, the DC is 8 plus your Charisma modifier and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB} bonus.

entries.name: Features
entries: Your Cohort improves and gains new features when you reach certain Captain levels, as shown on the Captain Features table.

entries.name: Proficiencies
entries: Your Cohort has proficiency in skills and saving throws listed in its statistics. Your Cohort uses your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} instead of its own. Because Cohort statistics already include a +2 {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, you need only adjust skill and saving throw proficiencies starting at level 5.

entries.name: Cohort Species
entries: When you initiate a new Humanoid Cohort, you can also give it one of the following traits to reflect its species.

entries.name: Dragonborn: Draconic Ancestry
entries: The Cohort has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to one of the following types of damage associated with its dragon progenitor (Captain's choice): Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison.

entries.name: Dwarf: Resistances and Immunities
entries: The Cohort has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Elf: Fey Ancestry
entries: The Cohort has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws it makes to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Gnome: Saving Throws
entries: The Cohort has proficiency in one of the following saving throws: Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma.

entries.name: Goliath: Powerful Build
entries: The Cohort has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any ability check it makes to end the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition. It also counts as one size larger when determining its carrying capacity.

entries.name: Halfling: Brave
entries: The Cohort has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws it makes to avoid or end the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Human: Skillful
entries: The Cohort has proficiency with one skill of your choice.

entries.name: Orc: Relentless (1/Day)
entries: When the Cohort is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it is reduced to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

entries.name: Tiefling: Fiendish Ancestry
entries: The Cohort has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to one of the following types of damage associated with its fiendish progenitor (Captain's choice): Fire, Necrotic, or Poison.

entries.name: Cohort Spells
entries: Throughout your adventure, you may wish to customize the spells listed in a Cohort's stat block. You can exchange one of the spells listed in the Spellcasting feature with another of the same level. Your GM decides if a spell is appropriate for a Cohort. Generally, the {@creature Priest|ValdaSpire24|Priest's} spells are from the Cleric spell list, the {@creature Mage|ValdaSpire24|Mage's} spells are from the Wizard spell list, and the {@creature Shaman|ValdaSpire24|Shaman's} spells are from the Druid spell list.

classFeaturesFull.name: Fighting Style
entries: You gain a {@filter Fighting Style feat|feats|category=FS} of your choice.
Whenever you gain a Captain level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.

classFeaturesFull.name: Captain Subclass
entries: You gain a Captain subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Captain levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Captain level or lower.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Blitz
entries: Once on each of your turns, you can direct your Cohort or an ally within 60 feet of yourself that can see or hear you. The chosen creature can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} or make one attack with a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Captain Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Valiant Surge
entries: Whenever you or your Cohort score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} or reduce an enemy to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you regain an expended Battle Die.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Cohort
entries: Your Cohort improves and gains a new feature.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Captain Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Coordinated Strike
entries: Once per turn when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action and hit with a weapon, you can deal an extra {@damage 2d8} damage to the target if your Cohort has dealt damage to that target since the end of your last turn. The extra damage is the same type dealt by the weapon.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Cohort
entries: Your Cohort improves and gains a new feature.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Captain Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Lead by Example
entries: Whenever you or your Cohort score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}, each ally you choose within 30 feet of you gains {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Cohort
entries: Your Cohort improves and gains a new feature.

classFeaturesFull.name: Teamwork Maneuvers
entries: When you use a maneuver that targets an ally, you can target a second ally within range without expending an additional Battle Die.

classFeaturesFull.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Legendary Commander
entries: Immediately after another creature's turn, you can choose yourself or an ally within 60 feet of yourself that can see or hear you to take a Legendary Action. This action is one of the following: {@action Attack|XPHB} (one attack only), {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, {@action Dodge|XPHB}, {@action Hide|XPHB}, {@action Magic|XPHB} (cast one cantrip only), or {@action Utilize|XPHB}. A creature can only take one Legendary Action each round. When a creature takes the {@action Dash|XPHB} or {@action Disengage|XPHB} action in this way, the benefits of that action last until the end of the creature's next turn.
You can use this feature to take three Legendary Actions and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Captain
entries: Decisive leaders and brilliant strategists, Captains inspire their allies to greatness. They stand alongside their Cohorts—their devoted lieutenants—whom they entrust with their lives. Captains out-strategize their enemies, ensuring that, while they rarely deal the killing blow, they're always on the winning side.

entries.name: Fearless Leaders
entries: A Captain thinks a little bigger than their compatriots, planning one step further and fitting their allies like puzzle pieces to the challenges ahead. To their eyes, there are few defeats; only setbacks, diversions, and detours. Success is always on the path ahead.

Moreover, Captains lead by example. They stand shoulder-to-shoulder with knights, creep through the night alongside rogues, and study arcane texts with mages, even when they barely understand what they're reading.

entries.name: Cohort and Commander
entries: A Captain is only as good as their second in command, their Cohort, who stands by them at every step and safeguards their plan's success. Far more than an ally, a Captain's Cohort is a confidant, an advisor, and a trusted friend. Cohorts see their Captain as a wellspring of information, and will follow them to the ends of the earth.

{@i Choose A, B, or C:} (A) {@item Chain Mail|XPHB}, {@item Shield|XPHB}, {@item Warhammer|XPHB}, 6 {@item Light Hammer|XPHB}, {@item Explorer's Pack|XPHB}, and 18 GP; (B) {@item Studded Leather Armor|XPHB}, 2 {@item Shortsword|XPHB}, {@item Heavy Crossbow|XPHB}, 20 {@item Bolt|XPHB}, {@item Crossbow Bolt Case|XPHB}, {@item Explorer's Pack|XPHB}, and 13 GP; or (C) 140 GP

classFeaturesFull.name: Expert Crafting
entries: Your experience at crafting items from raw materials grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Crafting Tools
entries: You gain a set of Crafting Tools, a combined toolkit that covers a broad range of applications. You can use these tools as any set of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB}. A set of Crafting Tools costs 75 GP.

entries.name: Instant Crafting
entries: You can take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to retrieve a piece of nonmagical gear from your belt, pack, cart, or wherever you keep your tools, even if you didn't have it in your inventory before. The item's cost must be no higher than 50 GP. You can't use this feature to produce a weapon, suit of armor, {@item Shield|XPHB}, or potion. An item retrieved in this way becomes lost in your inventory and vanishes when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can use this benefit twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Overnight Crafting
entries: When you take a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can craft nonmagical items whose combined cost in GP is no greater than your Craftsman level times 10. If an item's cost exceeds this number, you can complete it over multiple Long Rests; these rests needn't be consecutive. You must have the normally required tools and raw materials.

classFeaturesFull.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.
When you reach certain Craftsman levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Craftsman Features table.

classFeaturesFull.name: Masterwork Weapon
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can use your Crafting Tools and materials worth 50+ GP to improve a weapon into a Masterwork weapon. These weapons gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Masterwork Bonus
entries: The weapon gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls you make with it. This bonus increases as you gain Craftsman levels, as shown on the Masterwork Bonus column of the Craftsman Features table. If the weapon already has such a bonus, like a {@item +2 Longsword|XDMG}, you choose which bonus to use; you can't use more than one.

entries.name: Two Masterwork Properties
entries: You can add a second mastery property to the weapon from the "{@filter Mastery Properties|optionalfeatures|source=valdaspire24|feature type=mp}" section later in this class's description. The weapon must meet any prerequisite specified for the new property. If you choose the weapon with Weapon Mastery, you can use both of its mastery properties. You can change the second mastery property with a different one for which the weapon meets the prerequisites when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Other Creatures Wielding Masterwork Weapons
entries: Other creatures wielding your Masterwork weapons gain limited benefits. The creature gains half of the Masterwork Bonus, round up. If the creature can use the weapon's mastery property, it can use either of its weapon properties, but only one per turn. For example, if a Masterwork {@item Dagger|XPHB} has the {@itemMastery Vex|XPHB} property in addition to {@itemMastery Nick|XPHB}, a creature can choose to use {@itemMastery Vex|XPHB} or {@itemMastery Nick|XPHB} on its turn, but not both. If a mastery property has the [Craftsman only] tag, other creatures can't use that property.

classFeaturesFull.name: Fighting Style
entries: You gain a {@filter Fighting Style feat|feats|category=FS} of your choice. {@feat Defense|XPHB} is recommended.
Whenever you gain a Craftsman level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different {@filter Fighting Style feat|feats|category=FS}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Masterwork Armor
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can use your Crafting Tools and materials worth 50+ GP to improve a suit of armor into a Masterwork version. While wearing this armor, you gain a bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equal to half your Masterwork Bonus, round up. You can't use this feature to create Masterwork Shields. If the armor already gains such a bonus, like a {@item +2 Half Plate Armor|XDMG|+2 Half Plate}, you choose which bonus to use; you can't use more than one.

entries.name: Other Creatures Wearing Masterwork Armor
entries: Other creatures wearing Masterwork armor gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}. This bonus doesn't improve as you gain Craftsman levels.

classFeaturesFull.name: Craftsman Subclass
entries: You gain a Craftsman subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Craftsman levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Craftsman level or lower.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.

classFeaturesFull.name: Folded Steel
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can use your Crafting Tools to change a Masterwork weapon's damage type to one of the following: Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Piercing, or Slashing. You can't change a damage type that is a prerequisite for one of the weapon's mastery properties.

classFeaturesFull.name: Customize Armor
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can use your Crafting Tools to customize a suit of Masterwork armor with one of the following benefits. Any creature that has training with this armor can use this customization. You can replace this customization with another one when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Cast-Off
entries: You can doff this armor as a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Climbing
entries: While wearing this armor, you have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Diving
entries: While wearing this armor, you have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can breathe underwater.

entries.name: Integrated
entries: You can integrate a Simple weapon, Martial weapon, or {@item Shield|XPHB} directly into your armor when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can don or doff an integrated {@item Shield|XPHB} without taking an action once on each of your turns. When you draw or don an integrated item, it snaps to your hand, and you can't be disarmed of it. You can switch which item is integrated when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sleek
entries: This armor doesn't impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Craftsman Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Fortify Arsenal
entries: You can spend 10 minutes sharpening weapons and repairing armor, which can be done during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}. When you do so, choose one of the following benefits.

entries.name: Hone Weapons
entries: You can hone up to five weapons. A honed weapon has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls. Once a honed weapon deals damage, it is no longer honed.

entries.name: Reinforce Armor
entries: You can reinforce up to five suits of armor. A creature wearing reinforced armor has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. Once a creature wearing reinforced armor takes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, the armor is no longer reinforced.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Eye for Quality
entries: You can cast {@spell Identify|XPHB} and {@spell Locate Object|XPHB} without a spell slot or components. When you cast {@spell Identify|XPHB}, you also appraise the target item, learning its market value in Gold Pieces. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Craftsman Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Weapon Enchantment
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can place one of the following enchantments on a Masterwork weapon.
Only you gain the benefits of this enchantment. The enchantment on the weapon lasts until you use this feature to replace it with a different one.

entries.name: Blessed
entries: This weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d4} Radiant damage on a hit. This extra damage increases to {@dice 1d10} if the target is a Fiend or Undead.

entries.name: Elemental
entries: When you apply this enchantment, choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage. The weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d6} damage of the chosen type.

entries.name: Vampiric
entries: This weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d4} Necrotic damage on a hit. When you hit an enemy with this weapon, you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the extra Necrotic damage dealt by this enchantment.

entries.name: Venomous
entries: This weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d8} Poison damage on a hit.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Armor Enchantment
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can place one of the following enchantments on a suit of Masterwork armor. Only you gain the benefits of this enchantment. The enchantment on the armor lasts until you use this feature to replace it with a different one.

entries.name: Adamantine
entries: While wearing this armor, any {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against you becomes a normal hit.

entries.name: Cloaking
entries: While wearing this armor, you can take the {@action Hide|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks you make as part of the {@action Hide|XPHB} action during combat.

entries.name: Resistance
entries: When you apply this enchantment, choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder damage. You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the chosen damage type while wearing this armor.

entries.name: Winged
entries: While wearing this armor, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} until the end of your turn.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Craftsman Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Fabrication
entries: You can cast {@spell Fabricate|XPHB} without a spell slot or components. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Improved Masterwork
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Improved Enchantment
entries: Each of your Weapon Enchantments deal two extra dice of damage on a hit, instead of one.

entries.name: Third Mastery Property
entries: You can add a third mastery property to any Masterwork weapon. If you choose the weapon with Weapon Mastery, you can use all three of its mastery properties. Only you can use a weapon with three mastery properties.

classFeaturesFull.name: Spellwrought Armor
entries: While wearing Masterwork armor, you can add your Masterwork Bonus to saving throws that you make.

classFeaturesFull.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Irresistible Offense|XPHB} is recommended.

classFeaturesFull.name: Magnum Opus
entries: You create a Very Rare or Legendary magic item of your choice. You can only craft such an item once.

If the item requires {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you are instantly attuned to it and it doesn't count against the number of items you can attune to. You ignore all attunement requirements for the item. No other creature can attune to it while you are alive.
As long as you are on the same plane of existence as your item, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to call it to your hand or onto your body (as appropriate).

entries.name: Craftsman
entries: Craftsmen are virtuoso artisans and genius inventors. Not content merely creating masterwork pieces of weapons and armor, they invent and engineer ingenious devices and singularly deadly weapons.

entries.name: Master of Craft
entries: Artisans are integral to every culture: buildings must be erected, pots must be sent to the kiln, tools must be forged. Despite their pervasiveness, master craftsmen are as rare as they are prized. These creators and inventors can smith items of mythic quality and can solve most any problem simply by using the right tool and the appropriate amount of force.

entries.name: Secret of Steel
entries: Adventuring craftsmen come in many varieties, but nearly all leverage their advanced knowledge of metallurgy, smelting, and construction to forge arms and armor rarely seen, even by other adventurers. The smiths test their schematics and designs themselves, building prototypes and experimental gear that can later be refined into mass-produced items.

{@i Choose A or B:} (A) {@item Leather Armor|XPHB}, 2 {@item Dagger|XPHB|Daggers}, {@item Rapier|XPHB}, {@item Heavy Crossbow|XPHB}, 20 {@item Bolt|XPHB|Crossbow Bolts}, {@item Crossbow Bolt Case|XPHB}, {@item Dungeoneer's Pack|XPHB} and 17 GP; or (B) 120 GP

items: Gain the following traits from the Core Investigator Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency in one skill of your choice from the Investigators skill list, proficiency with Martial Weapons, and training with Light Armor.
Gain the Investigator's level 1 features, which are listed in the Investigator Features table

classFeaturesFull.name: Ritualist
entries: You have learned to cast {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB|Rituals} to overcome supernatural threats.

entries.name: Grimoire
entries: Your {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB|Rituals} are recorded in a grimoire, a Tiny object that weighs 3 pounds and contains 100 pages. You determine the grimoire's appearance and materials.

The grimoire starts with four level 1 {@filter Investigator spells|spells|class=investigator (VSS'24)} of your choice. {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB}, {@spell Heroism|XPHB}, {@spell Memorize|ValdaSpire24}, and {@spell Transient Bulwark|ValdaSpire24} are recommended.

Whenever you gain an Investigator level after 1, you can add two Investigator spells of your choice to your grimoire. The {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} Level column on the Investigator Feature table shows the maximum level of a spell you can add to your grimoire.

entries.name: Ritual Casting
entries: You can cast any spell as a {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} if that spell has the {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} tag and the spell is in your grimoire. You must read from the book to cast a spell in this way. You can't cast spells that are in your grimoire except as {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB|Rituals}, unless you've learned them by other means.

entries.name: Bonus Rituals
entries: You can treat specific spells as if they have the {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} tag, allowing you to add them to your grimoire and cast them as {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB|Rituals}. These spells are marked in the {@filter Investigator Spells list|spells|class=investigator (VSS'24)}.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Investigator spells.

entries.name: Expanding and Replacing a Grimoire
entries: The spells you add to your grimoire represent research into occult and supernatural threats, but you might find other spells during your adventures that you can add to your grimoire.

entries.name: Copying a Spell into the Grimoire
entries: When you find a level 1+ Investigator spell, you can copy it into your grimoire if it's of an eligible level and if you have time to copy it. For each level of the spell, the transcription takes 2 hours and costs 50 GP.

entries.name: Copying the Grimoire
entries: You can copy a spell from your grimoire into another book. This is like copying a new spell into your grimoire but faster, since you already know how to cast the spell. You need spend only 1 hour and 10 GP for each level of the copied spell.

If you lose your grimoire, you can recall from memory a number of spells equal to your Investigator level and use the same procedure to transcribe the spells into a new grimoire. Filling out the remainder of the new book requires you to find new spells to do so. For this reason, many Investigators keep a backup grimoire.

classFeaturesFull.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties} of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as {@item Rapier|XPHB|Rapiers} and {@item Heavy Crossbow|XPHB|Heavy Crossbows}.
Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

classFeaturesFull.name: Expertise
entries: You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. {@skill Arcana|XPHB} and {@skill Investigation|XPHB} are recommended if you have proficiency in them.
At Investigator level 9, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

classFeaturesFull.name: Finisher
entries: Once per turn when you deal damage with a weapon to a creature that is {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d8} damage to the target. The damage is the same type as the damage dealt by the weapon.
This damage increases as you gain Investigator levels, as shown in the Finisher column of the Investigator Features table.

classFeaturesFull.name: Rushed Incantation
entries: You can hastily perform any spell in your grimoire that has a casting time of an action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, casting the spell as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You can cast it without Material components unless the components have a cost of 100+ GP specified by the spell.

You can use this feature three times. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You gain additional uses when you reach certain Investigator levels, as shown in the Rushed Incantation column of the Investigator Features table.

classFeaturesFull.name: Investigator Subclass
entries: You gain a Investigator subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Investigator levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Investigator level or lower.

classFeaturesFull.name: Trinkets
entries: Your subclass grants you a number of supernatural trinkets to aid you in defeating supernatural threats and unraveling mysteries. You can use this feature twice, activating one of your trinket options each time you use it. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You gain additional uses when you reach certain Investigator levels, as shown in the Trinkets column of the Investigator Features table.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Exploit Weakness
entries: Once per turn when you deal damage to a creature with an attack using a weapon, you can target the creature where it is most vulnerable to gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Damage Vulnerability
entries: Choose one damage type dealt by the attack. The target has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to the chosen damage type for this attack. {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} from this feature doesn't double extra damage from spells (such as {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB}) or features from other classes (such as the Rogue's Sneak Attack). The {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} doesn't apply to this attack if the target has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the chosen damage type.

entries.name: Disrupt Resistance
entries: If the target has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to one or more damage types, it loses these {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} until the start of your next turn, including against the damage of the triggering attack.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Investigator Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Holy Trinkets
entries: You keep a wide array of {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB|Holy Symbols} and blessed items on your person, even if you aren't particularly pious. You can use the following trinkets (expending a use of your {@classFeature Trinkets|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|3} to do so).

entries.name: Amulet of Warding
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you place a divine ward on a creature of your choice within 60 feet of you. Until the start of your next turn, the warded creature gains a bonus to AC and saving throws equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

entries.name: Restorative Ankh
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, a creature of your choice within 60 feet of you regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Investigator level plus your Intelligence modifier.

entries.name: Rune of Banishment
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The creature must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC or be banished to a harmless location in the Ethereal Plane. While banished, the target has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0. At the start of your next turn, the creature reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Expertise
entries: At Investigator level 9, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Investigator Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Improved Finisher
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can use your Finisher on a creature that isn't {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, dealing only an extra {@damage 1d8} damage to the target.
At Investigator level 17, this damage increases to {@dice 2d8}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Enigma Arcane
entries: You learn a secret that unlocks potent arcane magic. You gain the ability to cast a level 7 spell, and discover additional secrets when you reach certain Investigator levels.

entries.name: Level 7 Spell
entries: You can cast one of the following spells without a spell slot and regain the ability to do so when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}: {@spell Mirage Arcane|XPHB}, {@spell Plane Shift|XPHB}, {@spell Reverse Gravity|XPHB}, {@spell Sequester|XPHB}, or {@spell Teleport|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Investigator Subclass.

entries.name: Level 8 Spell
entries: At Investigator level 15, you can also cast one of the following spells without a spell slot and regain the ability to do so when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}: {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB}, {@spell Glibness|XPHB}, {@spell Maze|XPHB}, or {@spell Mind Blank|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

entries.name: Level 9 Spell
entries: At Investigator level 17, you can also cast one of the following spells without a spell slot and regain the ability to do so when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}: {@spell Astral Projection|XPHB}, {@spell Gate|XPHB}, or {@spell Weird|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Supernatural Resolve
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects unless you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

classFeaturesFull.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Spellbinder
entries: Choose 5 Investigator spells in your grimoire of levels 1-3 that have a casting time of an action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You can use {@classFeature Rushed Incantation|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|2} to cast the chosen spells without expending a use of the feature, and you don't need to read from your grimoire to cast them.
Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace one of those spells with another spell in your grimoire.

entries.name: Investigator
entries: Supernatural detectives and monster slayers, Investigators are always on the hunt for malevolent outsiders. Whenever evil seeps into the world—be it Fiends, Undead, or strange Aberrations from beyond the stars—Investigators will be the first to locate them and banish their foul corruption from the mortal plane.

entries.name: Paranormal Investigators
entries: There are forces more ancient than time, foes more sinister than the foulest men, and beings more titanic than gods. Investigators risk their lives and psyches to protect the world from supernatural threats, unraveling the mysteries of one werewolf or demonic cult at a time. Their investigations are never ending, for victory only delays doomsday another night.

entries.name: Exorcists and Occultists
entries: To give themselves an edge against supernatural threats, Investigators dabble in forbidden magic themselves. Prepared Investigators keep a well-stocked grimoire of rituals, incantations, and notes on the powers and weaknesses of monsters—everything needed to level the playing field. Even so, an Investigator's occupation is perilous. A grimoire might spell out a vampire's fear of sunlight and aversion to silver, but it does little to hinder their fangs.

{@i Choose A, B, or C:} (A) {@item Scale Mail|XPHB}, {@item Shield|XPHB}, {@item Longsword|XPHB}, 6 {@item Javelin|XPHB|Javelins}, {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB}, {@item Priest's Pack|XPHB}, and 29 GP; (B) {@item Studded Leather Armor|XPHB}, 2 {@item Dagger|XPHB|Daggers}, 2 {@item Shortsword|XPHB|Shortswords}, {@item Longbow|XPHB}, 20 {@item Arrow|XPHB|Arrows}, {@item Quiver|XPHB}, {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB}, {@item Priest's Pack|XPHB}, and 11 GP; or (C) 170 GP

classFeaturesFull.name: Armor of Faith
entries: Your divine connection shields you from harm. You gain one of the following benefits of your choice.

entries.name: Anointed Armor
entries: You have training with Medium armor. While you are wearing armor, you can add your Wisdom modifier, instead of your Dexterity modifier, to your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}.

entries.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: While you aren't wearing any armor, your base {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Wisdom modifiers. You can use a {@item Shield|XPHB} and still gain this benefit.

classFeaturesFull.name: Spellcasting
entries: The gods demand that you sacrifice {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to cast divine magic.

entries.name: Hit Point Spellcasting
entries: To cast one of your level 1+ Martyr spells, you take Radiant damage to create a spell slot for that spell, which is immediately expended to cast it. The amount of Radiant damage you take is listed in the Damage column on the {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} Spellcasting table. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} and bypasses {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.
When you cast a Martyr spell, you choose the level of spell slot that you create, whose level is no higher than what's shown in the Max Slot Level column of the Martyr Features table for your level.

entries.name: Spell Uses
entries: When you cast one of your level 1+ Martyr spells, you expend one use of your spell uses in addition to taking Radiant damage. You can cast a total number of spells up to the number listed in the Spell Uses column of the Martyr Features table. You regain all spell uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Martyr spells. {@spell Command|XPHB} and {@spell Guiding Bolt|XPHB} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Martyr levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Martyr Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Martyr spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Max Slot Level column for your level.

If another Martyr feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Martyr spells for you.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace one spell on your list with another Martyr spell for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Concentration
entries: When a Martyr feature causes you to take Radiant damage, you don't make Constitution saving throws to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} as a result of taking this damage.

entries.name: Healing Magic
entries: Because your power is derived from mortal suffering, you can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} from any spell you cast.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Martyr spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use a {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Martyr spells.

classFeaturesFull.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties} of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as {@item Javelin|XPHB|Javelins} and {@item Longsword|XPHB|Longswords}.
Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

classFeaturesFull.name: Miraculous Healing
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can heal your own wounds. Roll one of your unexpended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} and regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the roll's total plus your Constitution modifier. This die is then expended.

As you gain Martyr levels, you can expend more dice each time you use this feature, adding your Constitution modifier to each {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die} you roll. The number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} you can expend equals half your Martyr level, round down.

classFeaturesFull.name: Reprisal
entries: When you take damage from a creature you can see within 5 feet of yourself, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to halve the damage taken. The creature takes {@damage 1d6} Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice).

entries.name: At Higher Levels
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} when you reach Martyr levels 5 ({@dice 2d6}), 11 ({@dice 3d6}), and 17 ({@dice 4d6}).

classFeaturesFull.name: Martyr Subclass
entries: You gain a Martyr subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Martyr levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Martyr level or lower.

classFeaturesFull.name: Sacrifice
entries: The gods demand that you undergo trials to curry their favor, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Sacrificial Strike
entries: When you deal damage to a creature with a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to enhance the strike. You take 5 Radiant damage and the target takes an extra 10 Radiant damage. This damage ignores your {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}, and bypasses your {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sacrificial Skill
entries: Once per turn when you fail a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can take 10 Radiant damage to gain a +5 bonus to that roll, potentially turning it into a success. This damage ignores your {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}, and bypasses your {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}. If the test still fails, you don't take this Radiant damage.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Martyr Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Sacrifice Foe
entries: When you make an attack or damage roll that is improved by your Sacrifice feature, and the attack reduces an enemy to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you don't take Radiant damage from using the feature.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Divine Respite
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can choose to regain up to 3 expended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
The number of expended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} you regain increases when you reach levels 13 (6 {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}) and 17 (10 {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}).

classFeaturesFull.name: Undying
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead and you can immediately use your Miraculous Healing (no action required).
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Improved Sacrificial Strike
entries: Your Sacrificial Strike improves. When you use this feature, you can choose to take 10 Radiant damage, and the target takes an extra 20 Radiant damage.
At Martyr level 17, the first time you use your Sacrificial Strike on each of your turns, you can do so without taking a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Divine Respite
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can choose to regain up to 6 expended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Martyr Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: March Unto Destiny
entries: You don't need to eat or drink, and have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Petrified|XPHB}, and {@condition Stunned|XPHB} conditions.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Divine Respite
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can choose to regain up to 10 expended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Improved Sacrificial Strike
entries: The first time you use your Sacrificial Strike on each of your turns, you can do so without taking a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Martyr Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Final Martyrdom
entries: You have at last reached your predestination: you will die in eternal glory. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can gain the following benefits for 10 minutes. At the end of the duration, you die. No force, short of a Cleric's Divine Intervention, can prevent your death, and you can't be returned to life by any means.

entries.name: Advantage
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests}.

entries.name: Immunities
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to all damage and to all conditions except for the {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Invisible|XPHB}, {@condition Prone|XPHB}, and {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Wish
entries: You can cast {@spell Wish|XPHB} once without a spell slot. You suffer no stress from using effects other than duplicating another spell.

entries.name: Quiet Martyrdom
entries: Not all stories of martyrdom end in dramatic confrontations with implacable foes. Occasionally a Martyr's sacrifice achieves a peaceful conclusion and satisfies the gods without costing their life. Nevertheless, the stories of these Martyrs still come to a close—they don't continue adventuring once their ultimate goal has been fulfilled. Perhaps they might retire to a distant hermitage, wander into the desert, or simply disappear into a crowd, never to be seen again.

entries.name: Martyr
entries: Martyrs are implements of the gods, handpicked to die in service of a divine cause. Such an end is inevitable, for once a martyr is chosen, their fate is fixed in the heavens.

entries.name: Fated to Die
entries: Martyrs are chosen by the gods, predestined to die for a great cause. They are prophets and oracles, great priests and liberators. Some Martyrs struggle against their destiny, but from the moment they are chosen, invisible strings of fate pull them onward. The gods may settle for a lesser Martyr if the one chosen is unwilling, but they always prefer to uplift their Martyr to the heights of sainthood before their inevitable demise.

entries.name: Sacrifice
entries: The gods invest their Martyr with deep wellsprings of power, but this power demands sacrifice. Drawing upon divine magic scorches a Martyr with radiance and wracks their body with pain. But the gods will never kill their charge early, and so offer healing in equal measure. Their Martyr shall meet their fate at the preordained time, and not a moment sooner.

{@i Choose A or B:} (A) 2 {@item Dagger|XPHB|Daggers}, {@item Rod|XPHB|Arcane Focus (Rod)}, {@item Robe|XPHB}, {@item Sack|XPHB}, {@item Shovel|XPHB}, {@item Scholar's Pack|XPHB} and 13 GP; or (B) 60 GP

items: Gain the Hit Point Die from the Core Necromancer Traits table.
Gain the Necromancer's level 1 features, which are listed in the Necromancer Features table. See the multiclassing rules to determine your available spell slots.

classFeaturesFull.name: Spellcasting
entries: Though it steadily burns away your very soul, you can cast necromantic spells.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know three Necromancer cantrips of your choice. {@spell Dancing Lights|XPHB}, {@spell Mending|XPHB}, and {@spell Ray of Frost|XPHB} are recommended. Whenever you gain a Necromancer level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Necromancer cantrip of your choice.
When you reach Necromancer levels 4 and 10, you learn another Necromancer cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Necromancer Features table.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Necromancer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 Necromancer spells. {@spell Exhume|ValdaSpire24}, {@spell Mage Armor|XPHB}, {@spell Ray of Sickness|XPHB}, and {@spell Silent Image|XPHB} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Necromancer levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Necromancer Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Necromancer spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Necromancer Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

If another Necromancer feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Necromancer spells for you.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you gain a Necromancer level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Necromancer spell for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Necromancer spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an Arcane Focus as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Necromancer spells.

classFeaturesFull.name: Charnel Touch
entries: You can draw upon an inner nexus of necromantic power. You have a pool of Charnel Touch points equal to 5 x your Necromancer level that replenishes when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can channel this negative energy through your touch. Choose a number of Charnel Touch points to expend, up to a maximum of 5 x your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and make a melee spell attack against one creature within reach. On a hit, the target takes Necrotic damage equal to the number of points expended. This damage is doubled without expending additional points if the attack roll scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. If the spell attack misses, the Charnel Touch points aren't expended.

classFeaturesFull.name: Thralls
entries: Unlike other spellcasters, you animate Undead creatures with a portion of your own life force, ensuring obedience.

entries.name: Animate Thralls
entries: You can animate Undead thralls by performing a ritual over the course of 10 minutes, which can be done during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}. The remains of one or more Medium or Small Humanoids within 30 feet of yourself rise as Undead creatures. These Undead become your thralls, and you maintain control over them indefinitely.

entries.name: Combat
entries: You can mentally control all your thralls without an action. If you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, your thralls will move to protect your body from harm, but won't attack.

In combat, your thralls take their turns immediately before or after your turn each round (your choice). All thralls collectively share one {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, which a single thrall can use each round.

entries.name: Attacks and Save DCs
entries: Thralls use your spell attack modifier for their attacks. If one of your thralls forces a creature to make a saving throw, it uses your spell save DC.

entries.name: Healing your Thralls
entries: You can use your {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1} on Undead under your control without making an attack roll. Instead of dealing Necrotic damage, the Undead regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the number of Charnel Touch points expended.

entries.name: Maximum Thralls
entries: You can animate and control one thrall that has a {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} of 1/4. As you gain Necromancer levels, you can animate more thralls. The combined CR of all your thralls can't exceed the number shown in the CR Total column of the Necromancer Features table, and the total number of thralls under your control can't exceed the number shown in the Thralls column of the Necromancer Features table.
At any time, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to sever your connection to one or more thralls. Corporeal Undead crumple into a heap and incorporeal Undead flee to the Ethereal Plane.

entries.name: Other Undead
entries: When you cast {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB}, {@spell Create Undead|XPHB}, or another spell that lets you create or control Undead, the Undead count as your thralls and can be commanded as such. If these thralls exceed your total {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} or number of thralls, you can immediately sever your connection to any of your existing thralls to stay within these limits. Your thralls can never command or create other Undead.
