As always, you can't reanimate Undead that have been reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. Your Animate Thralls ritual, the {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB} spell, and similar magic only affects Humanoid corpses, whereas your thralls are Undead creatures.

entries.name: Necromancer Variant Rules
entries: Use the following variant rules to tailor this class to your table and preferred playstyle.

entries.name: Necromancy Unleashed
entries: In order to ensure timely, balanced play, this class imposes limitations on the number of Undead a player can command, including with spells such as {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB}. Use this variant rule if you want to throw caution to the wind and embrace the undead horde experience.

Ignore the "Other Undead" section in the {@classFeature Thralls|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|2} feature. Undead animated with spells are separate from your thralls for the purposes of your class features, and have no other class-based limitations.

entries.name: Alternate Necromancers
entries: Necromancers may fuel their spellcasting through ambition or zeal, rather than intellect. When you become a Necromancer, you can choose Wisdom or Charisma for the Primary Ability in the Core Necromancer Traits table. The chosen ability becomes your spellcasting ability, and replaces any Necromancer feature which uses Intelligence.
A Necromancer that uses Wisdom is called a "Resurrectionist" and one that uses Charisma is called a "Ghoul."

classFeaturesFull.name: Dead Space
entries: You gain an extradimensional space that can hold up to 12 Medium or smaller corpses, piles of bones, or Undead creatures. The extradimensional space is linked to an item of your choice, such as a bag, a cloak, or a backpack. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can use the linked item to place a corpse, pile of bones, or willing Undead creature in the extradimensional space, or to dump out contents of your choice from the extradimensional space. {@classFeature Thralls|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|2} stored in your Dead Space count toward the total number of thralls under your control. The contents land in spaces of your choice within 5 feet of you, or as near to you as possible if those spaces are occupied.

You can link any item you can carry to the extradimensional space by performing a ritual over the course of 1 hour which can be done during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}. The previous item linked to the space becomes disconnected when you link a new one.

classFeaturesFull.name: Necromancer Subclass
entries: You gain a Necromancer subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Necromancer levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Necromancer level or lower.

classFeaturesFull.name: Dark Arcana
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a spell slot to replenish your {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1} pool. The pool regains points equal to your Intelligence modifier plus {@dice 1d8} for each level of the spell slot expended, up to a maximum of your pool's total.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Animate Dead
entries: You always have the {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB} spell prepared. When you cast this spell, its casting time is an action instead of 1 minute. You can also create a {@creature Spirit|ValdaSpire24} using the spell.

Additionally, when you cast {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB}, you can reanimate the corpse of any type of Medium or Small creature that isn't Undead, instead of only Humanoids.. The resulting Undead always uses the statistics of a {@creature Skeleton|ValdaSpire24}, {@creature Spirit|ValdaSpire24}, or {@creature Zombie|ValdaSpire24}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Critical Spellcasting
entries: Your potent Necromancy grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Critical Failures
entries: When a creature rolls a 1 on the {@dice d20} for a saving throw against one of your spells, it suffers a Critical Failure. It fails the save regardless of its modifiers or the spell save DC. If the spell deals damage, you roll all of the spell's damage dice twice and add them together, then add any relevant modifiers. This additional damage applies only to the creature that rolled a 1.

entries.name: Improved Critical
entries: Your spell attacks can score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Necromancer Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Improved Thralls
entries: Your {@classFeature Thralls|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|2} grow stronger under your control, granting the following benefits.

entries.name: Avoidance
entries: If one of your thralls is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

entries.name: Necrotic Damage
entries: Whenever one of your thralls deals Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can make it deal Necrotic damage instead.

entries.name: Turn Immunity
entries: Your thralls have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions, and are immune to effects that turn Undead.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Necromancer Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Improved Critical Spellcasting
entries: Your {@classFeature Critical Spellcasting|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|5} improves in the following ways.

entries.name: Critical Failures
entries: A creature suffers a Critical Failure when it rolls a 1 or 2 on the {@dice d20} for a saving throw against one of your spells.

entries.name: Improved Critical
entries: Your spell attacks can now score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20 on the {@dice d20}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Undying Servitude
entries: When one of your thralls is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cause it to drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead and regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Necromancer level.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

classFeaturesFull.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Lichdom
entries: You unlock the pinnacle of necromantic prowess, through which you conquer death itself: The Rite of Lichdom.

entries.name: Becoming a Lich
entries: The Rite of Lichdom is a ritual that you can perform over the course of 30 days in an isolated location. Once completed, your soul is bound to a spirit jar and you become a lich, an Undead of incredible power. You gain the following benefits, as well as those granted by your Necromancer subclass.

entries.name: Creature Type
entries: You are Undead. You are immune to any effect that turns Undead.

entries.name: Spirit Jar
entries: A spirit jar is an object that houses a lich's soul, safeguarding its immortality. If you drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, your body crumbles to dust and you reform after {@dice 1d4 + 1} days, reviving with all of your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. Your new body coalesces in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of your spirit jar. The new body is identical in every way to the one that was destroyed but has none of the original's equipment.

entries.name: Truesight
entries: You have {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet.

entries.name: Undead Immunities
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Necrotic and Poison damage and to the {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} and {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Spirit Jar
entries: A lich's spirit jar, or "phylactery," is as much a memento as it is their anchor to immortality, and as such, no two are alike. Spirit jars are often constructed from objects with sentimental value, such as family heirlooms or prized possessions, but can be fashioned from swords, pieces of armor, or even entire castles.

Furthermore, every spirit jar has a weakness, a critical flaw by which it can be destroyed, allowing its lich to be slain permanently. These weaknesses, too, are unique to each jar. One might require a ritual to be performed around it for 24 hours, while another might call for the jar to be dipped in the lava of an active volcano. Discuss with your GM the form your spirit jar takes and the weakness it possesses.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Necromancer Subclass.

entries.name: Necromancer
entries: Necromancers hold sway over the the forces of life and death, twisting them to serve their ambitions and commanding small armies of lifeless, animated thralls.

entries.name: Dark Souls
entries: Necromancers aren't gifted with the spark of magic. Rather, they turn to the most potent and dire source to fuel their powers: their souls. Each necromantic spell and enthralled Undead shaves away a miniscule part of their soul until only a spiritual husk remains, destined for no afterlife. This is a bargain they strike willingly—sometimes eagerly—in pursuit of an ambitious and terrible future.

entries.name: Grave Ambition
entries: Necromancers must match their grand intellects with an equal lack of scruples—the willingness to turn to forbidden knowledge and unquestionably evil methods. They are almost always driven by a deeper, darker impulse, a goal that pushes them to the utter brink. This might be the distorted ideal of a "greater good" or a goal to fix morality itself; in every case, Necromancy is a grim implement for their life's work.

entries.name: Masters of Undeath
entries: Trial and error teaches a Necromancer to puppet flesh, bone, and the spirits of the dead, binding them to their will. Unlike the Undead commanded by other spellcasters, a Necromancer's thralls are bound by the Necromancer's soul, leading to a small army of perfectly obedient minions that serve their master indefinitely.

{@i Choose A, B, or C:} (A) {@item Chain Mail|XPHB}, {@item Greatsword|XPHB}, 4 {@item Handaxe|XPHB|Handaxes}, {@item Explorer's Pack|XPHB}, and 15 GP; (B) {@item Studded Leather Armor|XPHB}, 2 {@item Scimitar|XPHB|Scimitars}, {@item Longbow|XPHB}, 20 {@item Arrow|XPHB|Arrows}, {@item Quiver|XPHB}, {@item Explorer's Pack|XPHB}, and 13 GP; or (C) 170 GP

classFeaturesFull.name: Secret
entries: For a reason that you keep utterly secret, you have committed to a life of endless travel. Choose this secret from the following options.

classFeaturesFull.name: Battle Tactics
entries: You learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called Battle Dice.

entries.name: Battle Dice
entries: You have two Battle Dice, which are d6s. A Battle Die is expended when you use it. You regain all expended Battle Dice when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} or finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Your Battle Die changes and more Battle Dice become available as shown on the Battle Dice column of the Vagabond Features table.

entries.name: Maneuvers
entries: You can expend Battle Dice to perform maneuvers. You learn three maneuvers of your choice for which you meet the prerequisites. {@optfeature Battle Edge|ValdaSpire24Extras}, {@optfeature Dig Deep|ValdaSpire24Extras}, and {@optfeature Rampage|ValdaSpire24Extras} are recommended. Maneuvers are described in the "{@filter Maneuver Options|optionalfeatures|feature type=mv:v}" section later on in the class's description. You gain additional maneuvers as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Maneuvers column of the Vagabond Features table. If another Vagabond feature gives you a maneuver, that maneuver doesn't count against your number of maneuvers known. Whenever you gain a Vagabond level, you can choose one of the maneuvers you know and replace it with another maneuver that you could learn at that level.

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries: If a maneuver requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.
When you reach certain Vagabond levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Vagabond Features table.

classFeaturesFull.name: Desperate Attack
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls while you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Breather
entries: As an action, you can expend one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, roll the die, and regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the roll plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}).

classFeaturesFull.name: Vagabond Subclass
entries: You gain a Vagabond subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Vagabond levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Vagabond level or lower.

classFeaturesFull.name: Overexertion
entries: If you have no Battle Dice remaining, you can regain one Battle Die to immediately expend it and use a maneuver or Vagabond feature. When you do so, you take Necrotic damage equal to one roll of the Battle Die. This damage ignores your {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}, and bypasses your {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Vagabond Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Mettle
entries: Your determination allows you to shrug off effects that would otherwise harm you. When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Last Stand
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead, and you regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Vagabond level.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Vagabond Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Desperate Fury
entries: While you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, your attacks with weapons and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} deal an extra {@damage 1d8} damage on a hit. The damage is the same type dealt by the weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Tenacity
entries: If you fail a saving throw to avoid or end a condition on yourself, you can expend one Battle Die to reroll the save and add the Battle Die to the roll. You must use the new roll.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Vagabond Subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Desperate Survival
entries: While you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB|Critical Hits} against you instead miss unless you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Deft Maneuver
entries: You gain a special additional {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} that you can take once on each of your turns. You can take this special {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} only to use a maneuver.

classFeaturesFull.name: Wayworn
entries: You are always considered {@status Bloodied|XPHB} for the purpose of your Vagabond features.

classFeaturesFull.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Irresistible Offense|XPHB} is recommended.

classFeaturesFull.name: Martial Recovery
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to regain all of your expended Battle Dice.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Vagabond
entries: A Vagabond's only home is the open road. Their endless journey would leave others dead on the roadside, but they endure through a desperate will to survive and a mastery of fierce combat maneuvers.

entries.name: Endless Wanderers
entries: Vagabonds drift between taverns and backwoods villages on an endless, wandering journey. Some choose the unrooted lifestyle, but many more were driven from their homes, never to return. Whether a particular Vagabond is a dangerous fugitive, penniless vagrant, or devout pilgrim is a secret known only to them. After all, anonymity is a precious boon for the road-weary.

entries.name: Desperate Maneuvers
entries: Their long journeys instill a feeling of desperation in Vagabonds. They're desperate to continue, to reach their destinations. But most of all, they're desperate to survive. When a Vagabond is backed into a corner, they fight like a crazed animal, slashing wildly, biting and scratching if necessary.

But they also learn more practical tools for survival. Vagabonds pick up maneuvers from traveling companions and warriors they encounter on their globe-spanning travels. Those who survive on the open road long enough accrue a deadly arsenal of combat techniques.
{@i Choose A or B:} (A) {@item Chain Mail|XPHB}, {@item Shield|XPHB}, {@item Warhammer|XPHB}, 6 {@item Javelin|XPHB|Javelins}, {@item Dungeoneer's Pack|XPHB}, and 15 GP; or (B) 130 GP

classFeaturesFull.name: Fighting Style
entries: You gain a {@filter Fighting Style feat|feats|category=FS} of your choice. {@feat Defense|XPHB} is recommended.
Whenever you gain a Warden level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different {@filter Fighting Style feat|feats|category=FS}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Sentinel's Stand
entries: You gain one of the following benefits of your choice. Whenever you gain a Warden level, you can replace the chosen benefit with another one.

entries.name: Stalwart Spirit
entries: You gain proficiency in one saving throw of your choice.

entries.name: Steadfast Toughness
entries: Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is increased by your Constitution modifier plus your Warden level. If you later replace this choice, your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum no longer receives this increase.

entries.name: Tower Shield
entries: While you are holding a {@item Shield|XPHB}, you have a +3 bonus to your AC instead of +2. At Warden level 10, this bonus increases to +4.

classFeaturesFull.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties} of two kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice, such as {@item Halberd|XPHB|Halberds} and {@item Longsword|XPHB|Longswords}. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Warden levels, you gain the ability to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties} of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Warden Features table.

classFeaturesFull.name: Guardian Tactics
entries: Your resolute fortitude allows you to hinder your foes and protect your allies using the following tactics.

entries.name: Block
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can choose one ally you can see. Until the start of your next turn, the ally's AC equals your AC if it is lower than that while the ally is within 5 feet of you. This effect ends early if you or the ally have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Challenge
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can goad an enemy that can see or hear you into attacking you. Until the start of your next turn, the enemy has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against creatures other than you while it is within 5 feet of you. This effect ends early if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Grasp
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can block the retreat of foes within a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you until the start of your next turn. A creature within the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} can't willingly move further away from you unless it first takes the {@action Disengage|XPHB} action. The {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} ends early if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

classFeaturesFull.name: Unyielding Resolve
entries: While you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

classFeaturesFull.name: Warden Subclass
entries: You gain a Warden subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Warden levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Warden level or lower.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.

classFeaturesFull.name: Interrupt
entries: When an enemy within 5 feet of you takes an action—such as Multiattack—that allows it to make multiple attacks or use additional abilities as a part of the same action, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to prevent one of its attacks or abilities. You take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} before any {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} is rolled for the action.
The enemy makes one fewer attack or uses one fewer ability than normal. You learn what attacks and abilities the enemy uses and choose which one to interrupt.

entries.name: Number of Uses
entries: You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} three times. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you reach certain Warden levels, you gain more uses of this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, as shown in the Interrupt column of the Warden Features table.

classFeaturesFull.name: Mettle
entries: Your determination allows you to shrug off effects that would otherwise harm you. When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Survive
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead, and you regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Warden level.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Sentinel's Strike
entries: You gain one of the following benefits of your choice. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace the chosen benefit with another one.

entries.name: Interdict
entries: When you use {@classFeature Interrupt|Warden|ValdaSpire24|5}, you can make a melee attack against the enemy as a part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}. Additionally, you regain a use of {@classFeature Interrupt|Warden|ValdaSpire24|5} when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}.

entries.name: Shield Slam
entries: Once per turn when you attack a creature within 5 feet of you as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action and hit with a Melee weapon, you can immediately bash the target with your {@item Shield|XPHB} if it's equipped. The target takes Bludgeoning damage equal to {@dice 1d8} plus the Shield's AC bonus.

entries.name: Sweep
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn using a Melee weapon, you can make an attack against each creature you choose within 5 feet of you, with a separate attack roll for each target, instead of attacking twice.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement

classFeaturesFull.name: Font of Life
entries: At the start of your turn, you can end one of the following conditions on yourself (no action required): {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, {@condition Stunned|XPHB}, or {@condition Restrained|XPHB}.
You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Extended Tactics
entries: The range of your {@classFeature Guardian Tactics|Warden|ValdaSpire24|2} increases to 10 feet: your Block affects an ally within 10 feet of yourself, your Challenge affects an enemy within 10 feet of yourself, and your Grasp is a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Improved Resolve

entries.name: All-Seeing
entries: You have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet. If you already have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB}, its range increases by 30 feet.

entries.name: Fortified
entries: No attack roll can have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} against you unless you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Unstoppable
entries: You can move through the space of any creature. Moving through its space doesn't cost you extra movement, but you can't stop in the same space. If the creature is your size or smaller, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition when you enter its space.

classFeaturesFull.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Legendary Resistance

You can use this feature three times, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Warden
entries: Armed with a shield and stubborn resolve, Wardens stand in defense of their allies and the innocent wherever they travel.

entries.name: Guardian's Call
entries: Every Warden hears a call to defend the helpless. Sometimes, they are directly called, such as when a village selects their mightiest member to defend them. Other times, they are compelled by more subtle means, such as witnessing uncontested injustice or feeling the weight of responsibility when tragedy occurs. The result is the same: Wardens who pick up their Shields and dedicate themselves to a charge.

entries.name: Strength of Champions
entries: A Warden's source of strength is their bottomless tolerance for punishment. Once they have adopted a group of creatures as their charge, a Warden might also reflect those particular strengths: a beastblood Guardian learns to hunt and roar with Beasts, and a Verdant Protector commands plants as a treant does.

classFeaturesFull.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned the simple, yet potent brand of spellcasting for which Warmages are known.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know four Warmage cantrips of your choice. {@spell Force Dart|ValdaSpire24}, {@spell Prestidigitation|XPHB}, {@spell Quickstep|ValdaSpire24}, and {@spell Shocking Grasp|XPHB} are recommended. Whenever you gain a Warmage level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Warmage cantrip of your choice. You can't replace a cantrip that is a prerequisite for a {@filter Warmage trick|optionalfeatures|source=|feature type=t}, unless you replace the trick at the same time.
You learn additional Warmage cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Warmage Features table.
If another Warmage feature gives you cantrips, those cantrips don't count against your number of cantrips known, but otherwise count as Warmage cantrips for you.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Warmage spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an {@item Arcane Focus|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Warmage spells.

entries.name: Cantrip Spell Level
entries: Due to their focus on cantrips, Warmages are extremely adept at punching through magical defenses. When you cast a Warmage cantrip, it counts as a spell of a level equal to half your Warmage level (to a maximum of level 9) for the purposes of {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Initiation
entries: Choose where you first learned the basics of magic.

entries.name: Making Your Own Initiation
entries: You can work with your GM to create an Arcane Initiation to suit your character's background. Choose two cantrips of your choice from any class's spell list; one cantrip should be suitable for combat, and the other for utility. Avoid choosing cantrips that are otherwise exclusive to another spellcaster. Also choose one skill.

classFeaturesFull.name: Warmage Edge
entries: Once per turn when you cast a {@filter Warmage cantrip|spells|level=0|class=warmage (VSS'24)}, you can improve the spell, gaining the following benefits.

entries.name: Intelligence to Damage
entries: Add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of the spell if you don't already add it.

entries.name: Improved Cantrip Upgrade
entries: Starting at Warmage level 5, you improve one damage roll of the spell, adding extra dice to the damage roll as shown on the Cantrip Bonus Dice column of the Warmage Features table.

classFeaturesFull.name: Reliable Cantrip
entries: When you cast a {@filter Warmage cantrip|spells|level=0|class=warmage (VSS'24)} at a creature and you miss with the attack roll or the target succeeds on a saving throw against the cantrip, the target takes the cantrip's minimum amount of damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip. You can apply {@classFeature Warmage Edge|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|1} to this damage (which also deals minimum damage), but you can't use this damage to trigger {@classFeature Warmage Tricks|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|2}. For example, if you cast {@spell Force Dart|ValdaSpire24} and miss, you can apply {@classFeature Warmage Edge|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|1} to deal Force damage equal to 1 plus your Intelligence modifier.

classFeaturesFull.name: Warmage Tricks
entries: You learn to use Warmage Tricks, special techniques that alter the way you fight, move, and cast your spells. You learn two tricks of your choice for which you meet the prerequisites. Warmage Tricks are described in the "{@filter Warmage Trick Options|optionalfeatures|source=|feature type=t}" section later on in the class's description.

entries.name: Prerequisites
entries: If a trick has a prerequisite, you must meet it to learn that trick. For example, if a trick requires you to be a level 5+ Warmage, you can select the trick once you reach Warmage level 5.

entries.name: Replacing and Gaining Tricks
entries: Whenever you gain a Warmage level, you can replace one of your tricks with another one for which you qualify. When you gain certain Warmage levels, you gain more tricks of your choice, as shown in the Tricks column of the Warmage Features table. You can't pick the same trick more than once unless its description says otherwise.

If you use this feature to improve a spell that has already scored a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}, the cantrip deals triple the number of damage dice in total.

You can use this feature twice. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You gain an additional use when you reach Warmage level 11.

classFeaturesFull.name: Tactical Insight
entries: You gain a bonus to saving throws against spells and other magical effects equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum bonus of +1). You don't gain this bonus to Intelligence saving throws.

entries: When a creature casts a spell that forces you to make a saving throw to avoid damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to attempt to redirect some of the spell's energy to a new target. If you succeed on your saving throw against the spell, choose another creature you can see within the spell's range or up to 30 feet away from you, whichever is closer, to make a saving throw against the spell, using your spell save DC. The chosen creature can be the original spellcaster. On a failed save, the creature suffers the effects of the spell as if you had cast the spell and it had been the original target or been within the area of the spell.

entries.name: Warmage
entries: Waving a black-and-red checkered banner, a dragonborn king charges into the fore. At his sides are Warmages of all houses, a chessboard of elite arcanists, poised to turn the tide of battle.
The undisputed masters of cantrips, Warmages turn the most fundamental types of magic into a deadly and precise art.

entries.name: Cantrip Masters
entries: While other spellcasters aspire to grander and more complex spells, Warmages refine and master the most fundamental magic: cantrips. Warmages wield their magic in the same way that a warrior uses a sword, bow, or axe—as weapons to be perfected, not as an unknowable force to be feared. In contrast to sorcerers and wizards, their magic is a trainable skill, one that can be mastered by almost anyone with discipline and aptitude. Therefore, Warmages stand among the most fearsome of spellcasters, with only the most rudimentary of spells.

entries.name: Strategic Geniuses
entries: Warmages have a long and storied history as masterful strategists and tacticians, both in grand battles and personal skirmishes. If a Warmage is outgunned or outmanned, they'll try to outthink their foes, which works more often than not. Warmages demonstrate an efficient kind of pragmatism, owing perhaps to their ability to solve many problems with just a few magical tools.

entries.name: Aligned Free Agents
entries: While some Warmages are fully self-taught, the majority join a house: a loose confederation of Warmages who practice together and share secrets of the trade. Houses teach invaluable battlefield strategy, but each individual house also touts their own brands of tactics and styles of magical tricks. The House of Knights, for example, emphasizes armor and martial prowess, whereas the House of Kings emphasizes battlefield strategy.

By way of metaphor, houses that value honor and teamwork above all else brand themselves after games of strategy, whereas those who epitomize self-reliance name themselves for games of chance. This division in the Warmage houses is representative of a schism that dates back to the earliest Warmage masters. Legend has it that the first two masters separated when one decided to found a college. The other, out of spite, built a casino outside its grounds.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Witch Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 spells from the Witch spell list. {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|XPHB|Hideous Laughter} and {@spell Thunderwave|XPHB} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Witch levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Witch Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Witch spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

If another Witch feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Witch spells for you.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you gain a Witch level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Witch spell for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Witch spells.

classFeaturesFull.name: Witch's Curse
entries: You are wracked by a terrible curse which infects your body and soul. Choose the form that this curse takes from the following options.

classFeaturesFull.name: Hexes
entries: You learn a number of powerful cantrips, known as {@filter Hexes|spells|level=0|class=witch (VSS'24)|subschool=hex}, derived from the same insidious magic that cursed you.

You know two Hexes of your choice from the Witch spell list, which don't count against your number of cantrips known. {@spell Hex: Misfortune|ValdaSpire24} and {@spell Hex: Ruin|ValdaSpire24} are recommended. Whenever you gain a Witch level, you can replace one of your Hexes with another Hex of your choice from the Witch spell list. When you gain certain Witch levels, you gain more Hexes of your choice, as shown in the Hexes column of the Witch Features table.

classFeaturesFull.name: Cackle
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to Cackle. When you do so, you extend the duration of one of your {@filter Hexes|spells|level=0|subschool=hex} by 1 round, provided the target of the Hex is within the spell's range.

Not all Witches laugh maniacally when they Cackle, but all Cackles require a Verbal component, as if casting a spell. These range from mundane curses and insults, to the murmuring of dead languages and speaking backwards.

classFeaturesFull.name: Familiar
entries: You always have the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it in 10 minutes without a spell slot or components. The spell is improved in the following ways when you cast it.

entries.name: Expanded Options
entries: You can choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: {@creature Death Snail|ValdaSpire24}, {@creature Flying Book|ValdaSpire24}, {@creature Homunculus|XMM}, {@creature Mock|ValdaSpire24}, {@creature Moon Jelly|ValdaSpire24}, {@creature Pet Rock|ValdaSpire24}, {@creature Pseudodragon|XMM} (can't use its Sting), {@creature Rag Doll|ValdaSpire24}, {@creature Tin Soldier|ValdaSpire24}, and {@creature Winter Wolf Pup|ValdaSpire24}.

entries.name: Synchronized Turns
entries: Your familiar takes its turn immediately before or after your turn each round (your choice).

entries.name: Quick Attack
entries: Once per turn as an action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can command your familiar to take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action (one attack only) on its turn.

entries.name: Spell Channeling

The familiar must be within 100 feet of you, and it must take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to deliver the spell when you cast the spell as normal.

entries.name: Witch Familiar

entries.name: Hit Points

entries.name: Your Spell Attack Modifier

entries.name: Your Saving Throw

entries.name: Your Proficiency Bonus

classFeaturesFull.name: Grand Hex
entries: You have perfected deeply malevolent forms of magic. You gain one {@filter Grand Hex|optionalfeatures|source=valdaspire24|feature type=gh} of your choice. Whenever you gain a Witch level, you can replace one of your Grand Hexes with another one.

classFeaturesFull.name: Vengeful Curse
entries: When an enemy you can see within 60 feet of yourself deals damage that causes you or an {@variantrule Ally|XPHB} you can see within 60 feet of yourself to become {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to curse the enemy. Until the end of your next turn, the cursed creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests}.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Hexmaster
entries: You have mastered your foul magic. When you cast a {@filter Hex that requires a saving throw|spells|level=0|class=witch (VSS'24)|subschool=hex|saving throw=strength;dexterity;constitution;intelligence;wisdom;charisma}, you can cause one target to automatically fail.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore one use of it by expending a spell slot (no action required).

entries.name: Witch
entries: Three old crones stoop over a boiling cauldron filled with all manner of bizarre filth, churning and bubbling with a noxious fume. In the smoke and vapor above the pot, the trio can make out shapes and figures of great import, and one cackles loudly at what she sees.

Witches are stricken by magic so dark it imprints a lasting shadow upon their essence. Through force of personality alone, they can spin this darkness outward, hexing creatures, casting manipulative spells, and even commanding a familiar with their thoughts.

entries.name: Cursed
entries: While others are blessed with magic, Witches are cursed by it. Afflicted by some hateful arcana, whether accidentally or intentionally, Witches are twisted inside and out by its daily tortures. With grueling effort, they can warp this power into spells to wrack others with the same magic that plagues them.

entries.name: Pariahs and Outcasts
entries: Almost without exception, Witches are feared and hated. They are victims of a number of misconceptions relating them to hags and other evil creatures of the night. As a result, known Witches are in great personal danger and can usually be found dwelling on the outskirts of civilization where townsfolk seldom tread. This does little to stop Witch hunting and burnings, but provides some measure of safety from them.

In reality, very few choose to become Witches, and many of them can hide adeptly in society, using their magic to fill a number of roles, from seer, to healer, to apothecary. Being accused as a Witch carries grave consequences, no matter the validity of the claim, so wise Witches relocate frequently, never residing in one place for too long.

weapons: Martial weapons that have the {@filter Finesse or Light|items|type=martial weapon|property=light;finesse} property

entries: {@i Choose A or B:} {@item Studded Leather Armor|XPHB}, 3 {@item Dagger|XPHB|Daggers}, 4 {@item Dart|XPHB|Darts}, {@item Whip|XPHB}, {@item Explorer's Pack|XPHB}, and 12 GP; or (B) 75 GP

classFeaturesFull.name: Dervish Fighting
entries: Your graceful movements and skill with nimble weapons grant you the following benefits.

entries.name: Deadly D4s
entries: Whenever you roll damage with a {@filter weapon|items|weapon damage dice=1d4;1d6} that deals {@damage 1d4} or {@damage 1d6} damage, you can deal {@damage 2d4} damage instead.

entries.name: Extra Finesse Weapons
entries: While wielding a weapon that deals {@damage 1d4} or {@damage 1d6} damage, it has the {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} property for you.

entries.name: Dancing with Firearms
entries: If using a Dancer in a setting with Firearms, the Dervish Fighting feature has the following additional benefit.

entries.name: Dervish Firearms
entries: Whenever you roll damage with a {@filter weapon|items|type=firearm|weapon damage dice=2d4} that deals {@damage 2d4} damage, you can deal {@damage 3d4} damage instead.

classFeaturesFull.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|XPHB}, your base {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Charisma modifiers.

classFeaturesFull.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as {@item Dagger|XPHB|Daggers} and {@item Hand Crossbow|XPHB|Hand Crossbows}.
Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

classFeaturesFull.name: Dance
entries: You can enter a flow state of Dance as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} if you aren't wearing Heavy armor. Your Dance lasts for 1 minute, or until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0, or you choose to stop dancing (no action required).

You can begin your Dance a number of times shown for your Dancer level in the Dances column of the Dancer features table. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Dance Die
entries: Your dancing prowess is represented by a Dance Die, which is a {@dice d4}. This die changes when you reach certain Dancer levels, as shown in the Dance Die column of the Dancer Features table.

entries.name: Graceful Dodge
entries: If a creature you can see hits you with an attack while your Dance is active, you can roll your Dance Die and add it to your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} against this attack, potentially causing the attack to miss you.

classFeaturesFull.name: Dance Styles
entries: When you begin your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2}, choose one of the following Dance Styles. You gain the benefits of this style until your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} ends or you switch to another one as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Agile Movement
entries: Your movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

entries.name: Elegant Form
entries: When you fail a Dexterity or Charisma check or a saving throw with any ability, you can add your Dance Die to the roll, potentially turning the failure into a success.

entries.name: Retaliatory Swipe
entries: Whenever a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack roll, the attacker takes damage equal to two rolls of your Dance Die. This damage is the same type dealt by a weapon you're holding or your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: Spinning Shot
entries: You can add your Dance Die to ranged attack rolls you make with weapons.

classFeaturesFull.name: Nimble Start
entries: Attacks against you during the first round of combat have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Dancer Subclass
entries: You gain a Dancer subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Dancer levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Dancer level or lower.

classFeaturesFull.name: Fast Movement
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Dancer levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeaturesFull.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.

classFeaturesFull.name: Three-Target Extra Attack
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can attack three times if all of your attacks are against different targets.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Dancer subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Evasion
entries: You can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain dangers. When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Heroic Dance
entries: When you begin your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2}, you can give yourself {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} if you don't have it.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Dancer subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Four-Target Extra Attack
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can attack four times if all of your attacks are against different targets.

classFeaturesFull.name: Graceful Retaliation
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself hits or misses you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make one attack against that creature, using a weapon with the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} or {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} property or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. Your attack follows the triggering attack and its effects.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Freestyle
entries: When you begin your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2}, you can choose two {@classFeature Dance Styles|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} instead of one. You can change one style at a time as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

classFeaturesFull.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Dancer subclass.

classFeaturesFull.name: Fierce Start
entries: Whenever you deal damage to a creature with a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} on the first round of combat, you can add your Charisma modifier to the damage roll.

classFeaturesFull.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Five-Target Extra Attack
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can attack five times if all of your attacks are against different targets.

classFeaturesFull.name: Invigorating Dance
entries: When you begin your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2}, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Dancer level plus your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1).

classFeaturesFull.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeaturesFull.name: Grand Finale
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action while your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} is active, you can perform a Grand Finale. Until the end of your turn, any attack you make that hits becomes a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}, and you can make two additional attacks as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. At the end of your turn, your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} ends.

You can't use this feature on the first round of combat, and once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending two uses of your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} (no action required).

entries.name: Dancer
entries: Masters of movement, Dancers leverage their unearthly grace and charm to glide unfettered through the battlefield.

entries.name: Elegant Performance
entries: Dance isn't merely a combination of rhythm and footwork. It is a Dancer's intrinsic expression, and, much like the careful somatic component of a spell, embodies a magic all its own. When a Dancer enters their flow state, they bound past lethal strikes and strike with a dramatic flourish, felling foes with a tempo that is at once elegant and fearsome.

entries.name: Nimble Combatants
entries: The elegant twirl of a Dancer's performance conceals a deadly momentum, unleashed at once with a flicker of blades or a spray of projectiles. Dancers are masters of nimble weapons, punching deeper and more precisely with a thrown Dagger than a Battleaxe. And when the battle reaches a crescendo, they can unleash a flurry of simultaneous strikes against a wall of unaware foes.
